bugs.desc: `julia-instantiate`, `update-julia` (:400), `doctor` (:405), `prod` (:218) and `stop` (:440) all run a bare `julia` and so use the shell's PATH. They never go through `_find_julia`. On a user-scope Apple Silicon install that got `<install>/juliaup`, running any of these from a terminal starts the user's Intel Julia under Rosetta, with no `JULIAUP_DEPOT_PATH`. To confirm, check whether user-scope installs are expected to run these tasks from a shell, or only through `pixi run app` → `app.py`

verify.evidence: pixi.toml:220 `prod`, :368 `julia-instantiate`, :372 `update-julia`, :377 `doctor`, :412-416 `stop*` all run bare `julia` from PATH. app.py:26-44 `_find_julia` is the only code that prefers `<install>/juliaup`, sets JULIAUP_DEPOT_PATH and puts it first on PATH, and only `pixi run app` reaches it (app.py:121, :241). install.sh:198-213 adds that juliaup on Apple Silicon user scope but never touches the user's PATH or shell profile (`--add-to-path=no`, :167). User scope writes no wrapper that exports PATH; only system scope does (install.sh:301-309). The docs that name these tasks are dev-checkout docs (docs/INSTALL.md:122,163; docs/SHIPPING.md:540-558), but runtime messages send installed users to `pixi run stop` / `stop-notebooks` / `stop-runner` (app/src/single_instance.jl:99, api/src/notebooks_api.jl:275, app/src/runner/server.jl:467).
verify.effect: In a user-scope install on Apple Silicon with an Intel Julia, `pixi run stop*` runs the Intel Julia under Rosetta. That still frees the ports, only more slowly, because portkill.jl only kills ports. `prod`, `doctor` and `julia-instantiate` would run the backend or Pkg under Rosetta, which is the wgpu/arch problem the native juliaup was added to avoid. The supported launch path (`pixi run app`) is unaffected.
verify.question: Are installed (user-scope) users supported running pixi tasks other than `app` from a shell, given that in-app hints tell them to run `pixi run stop`?
verify.recommendation: Treat `stop*` as supported for installed users, since the app's own error messages tell them to run it. Treat `prod`, `doctor`, `julia-instantiate` and `update-julia` as dev-only. `stop` works under Rosetta, so no code change is needed now. If you want it airtight, have user scope on Apple Silicon also add `<install>/juliaup/bin` to PATH and set JULIAUP_DEPOT_PATH in a launcher or profile snippet, the same way system scope's wrapper does. Or document in SHIPPING.md that only `pixi run app` gets the native Julia.

bugs.desc: , **brick_multi.wgsl:152** — `labColour`. `mip.wgsl` now treats a negative `p.lab.z` as a colour table: it returns `vec4`, and `labShown` skips labels whose alpha is 0. Both brick copies still clamp the row count with `max(i32(p.lab.z), 1)` and return `vec3`. If a negative row count ever reaches them, every label gets palette row 0 and hidden labels still draw. Nothing sends one today: `volumeRenderer.ts:1014` and `brickVolumeRenderer.ts` send `LABEL_PALETTE_N`, and the movie host only drives `mip.wgsl`. This is confirmed if Phase 5 (bricks for movies) sends `labelColours` through the brick pass.

verify.evidence: shaders/brick.wgsl:169-170 and shaders/brick_multi.wgsl:152-153: `labColour` returns vec3 and clamps rows with `max(i32(p.lab.z), 1)`, so there is no colour-table branch. shaders/mip.wgsl:109-124: a negative row count is read as a colour table, and `labShown` hides labels whose alpha is 0. Only two places write the brick uniform: brickVolumeRenderer.ts:1361 (`uniformCpu[BU.LAB + 2] = LABEL_PALETTE_N`) and volumeRenderer.ts:1011 (`LABEL_PALETTE_N`), both positive. No `labelColours` or other negative paletteRows writer exists anywhere in frontend/src.
verify.effect: Nothing visible today, because the brick passes only ever get the positive palette size. If a negative value ever reached them, every label would use palette row 0 and hidden labels would still draw.
verify.trigger: A brick renderer (for example a movie path running on bricks) writes a negative `lab.paletteRows` (a colour-table width) into the brick uniform. The fix at that point is to port mip.wgsl's vec4 colour-table `labColour` and `labShown` into brick.wgsl and brick_multi.wgsl.

bugs.desc: `_find_julia` runtime resolver. With this diff, the Julia install can now live next to a `juliaup` anywhere on PATH, for example `/opt/homebrew/bin` or `~/.local/bin`. `_find_julia` falls back only to `shutil.which("julia")` and then `~/.juliaup/bin/julia`. A desktop launch from a GUI often has a minimal PATH that leaves out that directory, so the app would not find the Julia the installer just set up. To confirm: check whether the user-scope launcher or desktop entry adds the user's shell PATH.

verify.evidence: app.py:26-44 _find_julia checks <ROOT>/juliaup, then shutil.which('julia'), then ~/.juliaup/bin/julia, and falls back to bare 'julia'. It never looks next to `juliaup`. install.sh:180-186 (user scope, from 7ac9446e) runs `juliaup add release` and sets JULIA=$(dirname $(command -v juliaup))/julia, e.g. /opt/homebrew/bin/julia. install.sh:376-401: the user-scope Linux .desktop runs `sh -c 'cd … && $PIXI run app'` and the macOS .app script runs `exec $PIXI run app`. Neither adds the user's shell PATH, unlike the system-scope wrapper (install.sh:308), which adds $JULIAUP_DEPOT_PATH/bin. `pixi run` only puts the pixi env's own bin first on PATH.
verify.effect: A user with a Homebrew juliaup or one in ~/.local/bin installs fine, then opens Cecelia.app from Finder/Dock. With launchd's minimal PATH, `julia` can't be found, the server never starts, and only ~/Library/Logs/Cecelia/launcher.log shows why. This also hits any reused `julia` outside ~/.juliaup. Fix: have the installer pass the resolved $JULIA to the launcher (env var or file) or bake it in, or have _find_julia check common juliaup directories.

also.desc: `_find_julia`, the launcher's Julia resolver. It is another copy of the Julia lookup this diff fixes in `install.ps1`, and it has drifted on Windows. Its fallback, `~/.juliaup/bin/julia`, has no `.exe`, so `os.path.exists` is false on Windows and it falls back to a bare `"julia"`. `install.ps1` checks `.juliaup\bin\julia.exe`. Whether this matters depends on how it's launched. The Start Menu `pixi run app` route probably has `julia` on PATH. A GUI launch whose PATH lacks the Store `WindowsApps` alias or the juliaup bin dir would not. Running `_find_julia` on Windows with no `julia` on PATH would confirm it

`_find_julia`, the private-juliaup check: it tests `<root>/juliaup/bin/julia` with no `.exe`. This hunk moves Windows system scope onto `<install>\juliaup\bin\julia.exe`, so on Windows that branch never matches. The function then falls through to `shutil.which("julia")`, and lines 44–45 have the same missing `.exe`. Through `cecelia-launch.cmd` it still works, because the launcher puts `$JuliaupDepot\bin` on PATH and sets `JULIAUP_DEPOT_PATH`. The rule SHIPPING.md cites ("applies the same rule for a launch that bypasses pixi") does not hold on Windows. A Windows launch of `app.py` that skips the launcher would confirm it.

bugs.desc: Julia resolver, user scope. It has the same shape as the bug this diff fixes. The script runs winget only when no `julia` is on PATH and `~\.juliaup\bin\julia.exe` is missing. It never checks `Get-Command juliaup`. If juliaup is installed but has no default channel, winget reports the package as already installed and does nothing. `$Julia` then falls back to a `.juliaup\bin\julia.exe` that doesn't exist, and nothing checks it the way `[ -x "$JULIA" ]` does in install.sh. To confirm: does a juliaup from the MS Store / winget always expose the `julia` alias, even with no channel installed?

verify.evidence: install.ps1:157 resolves `Get-Command julia`. install.ps1:158-160 runs winget (MS Store id 9NJNWW8PVKMN) only when that fails and ~\.juliaup\bin\julia.exe is missing. install.ps1:162 falls back to that path without checking it exists. install.ps1:214 `& $Julia` is the first use. The Store/MSIX juliaup registers both the `julia` and `juliaup` app execution aliases in WindowsApps no matter what channels exist. With no channel, the julia launcher sets up the default channel on first run. So Get-Command julia succeeds and the no-launcher state that B30 fixed in install.sh doesn't come up here.
verify.trigger: A juliaup on PATH that doesn't expose a `julia` command: the user turned off the `julia` app execution alias in Settings, or juliaup was installed via cargo or a portable zip without the launcher on PATH.

Double-clicking either one, or arming and confirming quickly, sends a `dblclick` up to the tab and starts a rename. This is the same gap the hunk closes in `SelectionTable` (`@click.stop` with no `@dblclick.stop`). To confirm: arm→confirm a tab close when `plotCount > 0` and see whether the tab is still in the DOM when `dblclick` fires, or double-click the duplicate button and see whether rename mode opens.

bugs.desc: `__cceceliaViewerCapture`, gated cell-track ribbon layers `(track) (${popVn}) Tracks ${p.path}`. These are still written as `{ visible: true }` with no `colour`, even though `rebuildOverlays` draws them as a track source under the key `${popMgrVn}::${pop.path}` (ViewerWindow.vue:~1655). The diff applies `drawn.get(key)` to `/_tracked` and trackclust layers only. So in track/speed mode the legend still shows the pop's colour for a ribbon drawn by track id or speed, and in solid mode with a user override it shows the pop colour instead of the override. That is the mismatch this fix removes for the other two layer kinds. This branch also still writes the layer when the ribbon stood down for trackclust (`suppressGatedForTrackclust`) or drew nothing, while `/_tracked` now checks `drawn.has`
bugs.why: not judged (the judge returned no verdict)

bugs.desc: `exportSvg` → `svgOf(host.value)`. This is the same bug the diff fixes, where a legend is dropped from the export, but by a different route. The export loses the colour legend, and for a numeric ramp the first `<svg>` may be the legend ramp itself rather than the chart

bugs.desc: Esc handler `ensureEsc`. It checks the persisted flag `settings.plotsMaximised`, which this diff now treats as different from "a maximised canvas is on screen" (`canvasMaximised`). On a page that isn't actually maximised (Settings, a page with no plots, or one with no active set) while the flag is still set, an Esc nobody else used still clears the flag. That silently drops the maximised layout the user would get back on the next module page. It is the same "flag ≠ real layout" shape that the `canvasMaximised` split fixes for `FloatingPanel` and `PointerBubble`. To confirm: decide whether Esc should restore the layout only while the layout is showing, or also clear a flag that persists across pages on purpose.

bugs.desc: `CellposeUtils.predict_slice`, both stitched branches (v3 + v4, `stitch_threshold > 0`). They hand per-Z stitching to cellpose's `utils.stitch3D`, which has the same bug this pin bump fixes in coastal's `match_masks_3d`: after an empty or non-overlapping plane, the next plane keeps its raw ids 1..k, so unrelated cells end up with one label. The fix for this (`split_z_gaps`, commit 35fb7cf8) is only on branch `fix-cellpose-stitch-ids` and is not an ancestor of HEAD. On this branch, the cellpose path still collides while the coastal path no longer does. This is cleared if `fix-cellpose-stitch-ids` merges to main before or alongside this change.

also.desc: (and the v4 branch at **:225**): `model.eval(..., stitch_threshold=..., do_3D=False)` sends 3D stacks through cellpose's `stitch3D`, which has the same bug that coastal #34 fixes in `match_masks_3d`. If a plane is empty before the first match, its ids are reused rather than renumbered. The fix for this (`35fb7cf8`, `split_z_gaps`) is only on the unmerged `fix-cellpose-stitch-ids` branch, not on `main` or this branch. So on this branch only the coastal half of the 3D-stitch collision gets fixed, and cellpose 3D runs still give unrelated cells one label

bugs.why: `fix/coastal-pin-match-masks` hasn't reached dacaa6b1

bugs.desc: `focusCapture` (`useCaptureFocus`), shape: an `agent_run` capture gets refocused in the viewer as if it were a capture the user shared. A Claude pointing at a run-record capture id would then open the viewer on an `imageUid` from the disposable copy, or return "Nowhere to reopen". To confirm: check whether a point target can carry an agent_run capture id (Claude sees them through the run record / `get_capture`) and whether those envelopes carry `address.imageUid`

bugs.desc: `sweep` hit-again update (`c["key"] in carried`) vs. the `known` set built from `sources`. An agent-run error that has a `file:line` goes through the judge path, so `_merge` can fold it into a fanout finding on the same file + function. The carried bug is then keyed by the lead's key, and the agent-run key only appears in `sources`. On the next pass that key is in `known`, so the error is not raised as new, but it is also not in `carried`, so `runs` / `last_seen` are never updated. The carry predicate `b.get("kind") == "agent_run" and status in MUTED` has the same gap: a merged bug led by a fanout finding is never muted. To confirm, check whether the merged dict can have a fanout `kind` with an agent-run key in `sources`. Per `_merge`, `{**lead, ...}` keeps the lead's kind, so it can.
bugs.why: `judge-agent-run-findings` hasn't reached dacaa6b1
